title: Re-enable Java compiler warnings and add static analysis
description:
The Java build still has a large static-analysis gap:
- Root `pom.xml` comments out `<compilerArgument>-Xlint:all</compilerArgument>`.
- Only `Mage.Verify/pom.xml` and `Mage.Tests/pom.xml` enable `-Xlint:unchecked` today.
- There is still no Checkstyle, SpotBugs, Error Prone, PMD, or similar plugin wired into `make check`.

A fresh suppression scan found the existing warning backlog is not theoretical:
- 98 `@SuppressWarnings(...)` annotations across the Java tree
- 11 `//noinspection ...` comments
- Most suppressions are `unchecked` in Swing/client code, plus a smaller number of `rawtypes`, `unused`, `deprecation`, and `null`

That means tightening Java linting is worth doing, but it should be staged instead of flipping `-Xlint:all` repo-wide in one shot. Suggested path:
1. Re-enable a conservative `javac` warning set first, likely `-Xlint:unchecked,deprecation`.
2. Measure warning volume module-by-module, especially `Mage.Client.Bridge`, `Mage.Common`, and the client UI modules where most suppressions live.
3. Once the baseline is understood, add a real static-analysis tool to `make check` if the false-positive rate is acceptable.

The goal is to surface real API misuse and unsafe generics issues in normal development instead of relying only on runtime behavior and code review.
